scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: Scene II. Mytilene. A room in a brothel.
scene.location: Mytilene. A room in a brothel.

lines.text: Boult!
lines.plainText: Boult

lines.text: Sir?
lines.plainText: Sir

lines.text: Search the market narrowly; Mytilene is full of gallants. We lost too much money this mart by being too wenchless.
lines.plainText: Search the market narrowly Mytilene is full of gallants We lost too much money this mart by being too wenchless

lines.text: We were never so much out of creatures. We have but poor three, and they can do no more than they can do; and they with continual action are even as good as rotten.
lines.plainText: We were never so much out of creatures We have but poor three and they can do no more than they can do and they with continual action are even as good as rotten

lines.text: Therefore let's have fresh ones, whate'er we pay for them. If there be not a conscience to be used in every trade, we shall never prosper.
lines.plainText: Therefore let's have fresh ones whate'er we pay for them If there be not a conscience to be used in every trade we shall never prosper

lines.text: Thou sayest true: 'tis not our bringing up of poor bastards,—as, I think, I have brought up some eleven—
lines.plainText: Thou sayest true 'tis not our bringing up of poor bastardsas I think I have brought up some eleven

lines.text: Ay, to eleven; and brought them down again. But shall I search the market?
lines.plainText: Ay to eleven and brought them down again But shall I search the market

lines.text: What else, man? The stuff we have, a strong wind will blow it to pieces, they are so pitifully sodden.
lines.plainText: What else man The stuff we have a strong wind will blow it to pieces they are so pitifully sodden

lines.text: Thou sayest true; they're too unwholesome, o' conscience. The poor Transylvanian is dead, that lay with the little baggage.
lines.plainText: Thou sayest true they're too unwholesome o' conscience The poor Transylvanian is dead that lay with the little baggage

lines.text: Ay, she quickly pooped him; she made him roast-meat for worms. But I'll go search the market.
lines.plainText: Ay she quickly pooped him she made him roastmeat for worms But I'll go search the market

lines.text: Three or four thousand chequins were as pretty a proportion to live quietly, and so give over.
lines.plainText: Three or four thousand chequins were as pretty a proportion to live quietly and so give over

lines.text: Why to give over, I pray you? Is it a shame to get when we are old?
lines.plainText: Why to give over I pray you Is it a shame to get when we are old

lines.text: O, our credit comes not in like the commodity, nor the commodity wages not with the danger: therefore, if in our youths we could pick up some pretty estate, 'twere not amiss to keep our door hatched. Besides, the sore terms we stand upon with the gods will be strong with us for giving over.
lines.plainText: O our credit comes not in like the commodity nor the commodity wages not with the danger therefore if in our youths we could pick up some pretty estate 'twere not amiss to keep our door hatched Besides the sore terms we stand upon with the gods will be strong with us for giving over

lines.text: Come, others sorts offend as well as we.
lines.plainText: Come others sorts offend as well as we

lines.text: As well as we! ay, and better too; we offend worse. Neither is our profession any trade; it's no calling. But here comes Boult.
lines.plainText: As well as we ay and better too we offend worse Neither is our profession any trade it's no calling But here comes Boult

content.text: Re-enter Boult, with the Pirates and Marina.

lines.text: [To Pirates.] Come your ways. My masters, you say she's a virgin?
lines.plainText: To Pirates Come your ways My masters you say she's a virgin

lines.text: O sir, we doubt it not.
lines.plainText: O sir we doubt it not

lines.text: Master, I have gone through for this piece, you see: if you like her, so; if not, I have lost my earnest.
lines.plainText: Master I have gone through for this piece you see if you like her so if not I have lost my earnest

lines.text: Boult, has she any qualities?
lines.plainText: Boult has she any qualities

lines.text: She has a good face, speaks well and has excellent good clothes: there's no farther necessity of qualities can make her be refused.
lines.plainText: She has a good face speaks well and has excellent good clothes there's no farther necessity of qualities can make her be refused

lines.text: What is her price, Boult?
lines.plainText: What is her price Boult

lines.text: I cannot be baited one doit of a thousand pieces.
lines.plainText: I cannot be baited one doit of a thousand pieces

lines.text: Well, follow me, my masters, you shall have your money presently. Wife, take her in; instruct her what she has to do, that she may not be raw in her entertainment.
lines.plainText: Well follow me my masters you shall have your money presently Wife take her in instruct her what she has to do that she may not be raw in her entertainment

lines.text: Boult, take you the marks of her, the colour of her hair, complexion, height, her age, with warrant of her virginity; and cry 'He that will give most shall have her first.' Such a maidenhead were no cheap thing, if men were as they have been. Get this done as I command you.
lines.plainText: Boult take you the marks of her the colour of her hair complexion height her age with warrant of her virginity and cry 'He that will give most shall have her first' Such a maidenhead were no cheap thing if men were as they have been Get this done as I command you

lines.text: Performance shall follow.
lines.plainText: Performance shall follow

lines.text: Alack that Leonine was so slack, so slow!
lines.plainText: Alack that Leonine was so slack so slow

lines.text: He should have struck, not spoke; or that these pirates,
lines.plainText: He should have struck not spoke or that these pirates

lines.text: Not enough barbarous, had not o'erboard thrown me
lines.plainText: Not enough barbarous had not o'erboard thrown me

lines.text: For to seek my mother!
lines.plainText: For to seek my mother

lines.text: Why lament you, pretty one?
lines.plainText: Why lament you pretty one

lines.text: That I am pretty.
lines.plainText: That I am pretty

lines.text: Come, the gods have done their part in you.
lines.plainText: Come the gods have done their part in you

lines.text: I accuse them not.
lines.plainText: I accuse them not

lines.text: You are light into my hands, where you are like to live.
lines.plainText: You are light into my hands where you are like to live

lines.text: The more my fault
lines.plainText: The more my fault

lines.text: To scape his hands where I was like to die.
lines.plainText: To scape his hands where I was like to die

lines.text: Ay, and you shall live in pleasure.
lines.plainText: Ay and you shall live in pleasure

lines.text: No.
lines.plainText: No

lines.text: Yes, indeed shall you, and taste gentlemen of all fashions: you shall fare well; you shall have the difference of all complexions. What! do you stop your ears?
lines.plainText: Yes indeed shall you and taste gentlemen of all fashions you shall fare well you shall have the difference of all complexions What do you stop your ears

lines.text: Are you a woman?
lines.plainText: Are you a woman

lines.text: What would you have me be, an I be not a woman?
lines.plainText: What would you have me be an I be not a woman

lines.text: An honest woman, or not a woman.
lines.plainText: An honest woman or not a woman

lines.text: Marry, whip the gosling: I think I shall have something to do with you. Come, you're a young foolish sapling, and must be bowed as I would have you.
lines.plainText: Marry whip the gosling I think I shall have something to do with you Come you're a young foolish sapling and must be bowed as I would have you

lines.text: The gods defend me!
lines.plainText: The gods defend me

lines.text: If it please the gods to defend you by men, then men must comfort you, men must feed you, men stir you up. Boult's returned.
lines.plainText: If it please the gods to defend you by men then men must comfort you men must feed you men stir you up Boult's returned

lines.text: I have cried her almost to the number of her hairs; I have drawn her picture with my voice.
lines.plainText: I have cried her almost to the number of her hairs I have drawn her picture with my voice

lines.text: And I prithee tell me, how dost thou find the inclination of the people, especially of the younger sort?
lines.plainText: And I prithee tell me how dost thou find the inclination of the people especially of the younger sort

lines.text: Faith, they listened to me as they would have hearkened to their father's testament. There was a Spaniard's mouth so watered, that he went to bed to her very description.
lines.plainText: Faith they listened to me as they would have hearkened to their father's testament There was a Spaniard's mouth so watered that he went to bed to her very description

lines.text: We shall have him here tomorrow with his best ruff on.
lines.plainText: We shall have him here tomorrow with his best ruff on

lines.text: Tonight, tonight. But, mistress, do you know the French knight that cowers i' the hams?
lines.plainText: Tonight tonight But mistress do you know the French knight that cowers i' the hams

lines.text: Who, Monsieur Veroles?
lines.plainText: Who Monsieur Veroles

lines.text: Ay, he: he offered to cut a caper at the proclamation; but he made a groan at it, and swore he would see her tomorrow.
lines.plainText: Ay he he offered to cut a caper at the proclamation but he made a groan at it and swore he would see her tomorrow

lines.text: Well, well, as for him, he brought his disease hither: here he does but repair it. I know he will come in our shadow, to scatter his crowns in the sun.
lines.plainText: Well well as for him he brought his disease hither here he does but repair it I know he will come in our shadow to scatter his crowns in the sun

lines.text: Well, if we had of every nation a traveller, we should lodge them with this sign.
lines.plainText: Well if we had of every nation a traveller we should lodge them with this sign

lines.text: I understand you not.
lines.plainText: I understand you not

lines.text: O, take her home, mistress, take her home: these blushes of hers must be quenched with some present practice.
lines.plainText: O take her home mistress take her home these blushes of hers must be quenched with some present practice

lines.text: Thou sayest true, i'faith so they must; for your bride goes to that with shame which is her way to go with warrant.
lines.plainText: Thou sayest true i'faith so they must for your bride goes to that with shame which is her way to go with warrant

lines.text: Faith, some do and some do not. But, mistress, if I have bargained for the joint,—
lines.plainText: Faith some do and some do not But mistress if I have bargained for the joint

lines.text: Thou mayst cut a morsel off the spit.
lines.plainText: Thou mayst cut a morsel off the spit

lines.text: I may so.
lines.plainText: I may so

lines.text: Who should deny it? Come young one, I like the manner of your garments well.
lines.plainText: Who should deny it Come young one I like the manner of your garments well

lines.text: Ay, by my faith, they shall not be changed yet.
lines.plainText: Ay by my faith they shall not be changed yet

lines.text: Boult, spend thou that in the town: report what a sojourner we have; you'll lose nothing by custom. When nature framed this piece, she meant thee a good turn; therefore say what a paragon she is, and thou hast the harvest out of thine own report.
lines.plainText: Boult spend thou that in the town report what a sojourner we have you'll lose nothing by custom When nature framed this piece she meant thee a good turn therefore say what a paragon she is and thou hast the harvest out of thine own report

lines.text: I warrant you, mistress, thunder shall not so awake the beds of eels as my giving out her beauty stirs up the lewdly inclined. I'll bring home some tonight.
lines.plainText: I warrant you mistress thunder shall not so awake the beds of eels as my giving out her beauty stirs up the lewdly inclined I'll bring home some tonight

lines.text: Come your ways; follow me.
lines.plainText: Come your ways follow me

lines.text: If fires be hot, knives sharp, or waters deep,
lines.plainText: If fires be hot knives sharp or waters deep

lines.text: Untied I still my virgin knot will keep.
lines.plainText: Untied I still my virgin knot will keep

lines.text: Diana, aid my purpose!
lines.plainText: Diana aid my purpose

lines.text: What have we to do with Diana? Pray you, will you go with us?
lines.plainText: What have we to do with Diana Pray you will you go with us
